memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease.
Patient reports burning retrosternal pain after meals, occasional regurgitation, and nighttime cough. On examination, mild epigastric tenderness, no oral thrush, lungs clear. She is a former smoker (10 pack-years, quit 2018).

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Pantoprazole 40 mg orally once daily before breakfast
Domperidone 10 mg orally twice daily before meals
Antacid gel as needed after meals

memories.author: lab
memories.text: H. pylori stool antigen: Negative (reference: <0.9 IU/mL).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Still getting heartburn after spicy food, especially at night. Taking pantoprazole most days but sometimes forget domperidone.

memories.author: D05
memories.text:
Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease, partially controlled.
Symptoms improved: heartburn 2-3 times/week, less regurgitation. No alarm features. Abdomen soft, no tenderness. Former smoker, quit 2018, 10 pack-years.

memories.author: D05

Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease with worsening symptoms.
Heartburn daily, nocturnal regurgitation, occasional dyspepsia. Mild epigastric tenderness, no weight loss. Former smoker, quit 2018, 10 pack-years.

memories.author: D05

memories.author: D05
memories.text: Upper GI endoscopy: Mild erosive esophagitis (Los Angeles grade A) in distal esophagus, no Barrett's epithelium. H. pylori negative on biopsy.

memories.author: D05

Post-endoscopy review: GERD improving.
Heartburn now 1-2 times/week, no nocturnal symptoms. Abdomen benign. Former smoker, quit 2018, 10 pack-years.
